text:
maria_support: FYI ACME reporting persistent 429s on their Dedicated pool since the plan migration at ~09:00 UTC. They say throughput dropped even though tokens billed are high. Can SRE/infra look?

aj_sre: Can you paste the exact 429 response (headers + any X-Quota-* values)? Also need tenant id and route.

maria_support: Tenant: acme-corp (tenant_id=tenant_8242). Route: /v1/generate. Example curl and response we captured: 
```bash
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rw-v1","input":"hello"}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:34 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
X-Quota-Remaining: -3
X-Quota-Limit: 120
X-Quota-Unit: hour
Content-Length: 128

{"error":"rate limit exceeded","code":429} 
```
They attached a billing screenshot showing normal usage but app sees 429s.

liam_infra: Negative X-Quota-Remaining is interesting. That suggests multiple quota records or a unit mismatch. Did we recently migrate plan for tenant_8242?

maria_support: Yes, they did a plan migration yesterday to a reserved Dedicated bundle. Support updated billing, but I think a few config entries were changed in the quota service around midnight.

aj_sre: I'm going to query quota-store for tenant_8242, looking for duplicate keys or different units. Back in a sec.

aj_sre: (query result pasted) 
```text
-- quota-store rows for tenant_8242 --
row1: key=tenant:tenant_8242:rate, limit=120, unit=hour, source=legacy-billing, created=2025-11-02T23:58:10Z
row2: key=tenant:tenant_8242:rate, limit=2, unit=minute, source=plan-migrate, created=2026-02-10T00:12:01Z
row3: key=tenant:tenant_8242:burst, limit=30, unit=minute, source=reserved-profiles, created=2026-02-10T00:12:03Z
```
Looks like we have both hour and minute rows for same logical rate key. Quota merge logic should prefer the most recent source but it appears the runtime is summing limits and using hour unit for headers. That explains high billing tokens but quick throttles.

sophia_eng: That mismatch would cause weird remaining values since the aggregator converts units to a canonical base incorrectly if duplicates exist. I suspect the cache didn't evict, so runtime read stale 'hour' record plus new minute record.

liam_infra: Autoscaler logs for the dedicated pool show no scale events for tenant_8242. There's a flag in the pool binding: allow_burst=false after migration. If allow_burst=false we won't use burst capacity and per-tenant pacing is stricter. Combined with conflicting quota rows this will throttle earlier.

maria_support: Customer is complaining that they were charged for tokens during the spike but calls are 429ing. Need to get them unblocked ASAP. Can we do a quick temporary override to lift throttles while we fix the entries?

aj_sre: Yes. I can add a temporary override rule (support-override: unlimited for 10m) but need approval from ops. ops-bot, approve?

ops-bot: @aj_sre please file a stabilizing incident and get a senior approval for overrides. Tagging @maria_support and @liam_infra.

maria_support: Filed INC-2026-487 in ops. Customer-facing message drafted and sent: "We're investigating rate-limit anomalies, temporary allowance applied while we fix backend config."

aj_sre: While ops approves, here's a safe quick mitigation: delete the legacy-billing hour-row or set its limit to 0 in quota-store for tenant_8242, then flush quota-cache on runtime nodes. I'll run the commands in the maintenance window immediately after approval.

sophia_eng: Agreed. Also need to ensure quota-merge logic doesn't re-create the duplicate on background sync. Create a migration script that normalizes units (prefer plan-migrate entries and convert minute->hour or vice versa according to canonical unit) and add a validation check to the plan migration flow.

liam_infra: I'll flip allow_burst=true temporarily on the pool binding to let autoscaler use burst capacity (will reduce observed 429s while we scrub quota rows). Then we can revert once normalized.

aj_sre: ops approved emergency override for 20m (logged). Executing: 
```bash
# remove legacy hour row
quotactl delete --tenant tenant_8242 --key rate --source legacy-billing || true
# flush cache on runtime nodes
for node in runtime-1 runtime-2 runtime-3; do ssh $node 'systemctl restart redwood-quota-cache' & done
```

maria_support: Customer just confirmed errors dropping, latency back to normal. They see no more 429s in last 4 minutes. They still want to confirm billing alignment.

sophia_eng: I'll push a small migration to remove duplicates and add validation tests (deploy in ~30m). Also push a fix so quota-merge treats plan-migrate as authoritative.

aj_sre: After cache flush I see X-Quota-Remaining headers behaving: X-Quota-Remaining: 47, X-Quota-Limit: 120, X-Quota-Unit: hour. No negatives.

liam_infra: Reverted allow_burst to previous value but autoscaler policy will be tuned to prevent brittle throttles.

maria_support: Customer pleased with the quick turnaround. They've asked for a postmortem and billing reconciliation. I've scheduled handoff to billing ops for invoice review.

sophia_eng: Postmortem TODOs: 1) migration flow unit validation 2) quota-store dedupe job 3) improve runtime detection for duplicate quota rows 4) add alert when X-Quota-Remaining < 0 5) add end-to-end test for plan migration.

aj_sre: Resolved for now. Will update INC-2026-487 with steps and timelines. Closing thread when migration shipped. :white_check_mark:
